newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca, Oncotech to work on prostate cancer.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca, Oncotech to work on prostate cancer.

text.p: British bioscience company Zeneca Group Plc said on Wednesday that it is to work with U.S. cancer specialist Oncotech Inc to improve the treatment of prostate cancer.
In a statement, Zeneca said the two companies planned to develop a test which doctors would be able to use, initially in the U.S, to choose the best treatment available for each patient.
It said the two sides will seek "to understand more clearly why some patients with prostate cancer respond better than others to the same treatments."

The work will aim to "discover and understand selected genetic changes within prostate cancer", and then develop new diagnostic tests. Both sides said the cooperation would be extended to developing genetic tests for other forms of cancer.
Zeneca said prostate cancer is the most common form of cancer among men in the U.S, with 317,000 new cases diagnosed every year and 41,400 deaths.

Zeneca Diagnostics general manager Philip Webb said cancer treatment would improve in the future through more precise diagnosis of the characteristics of an individual tumour and more targeted treatment.
Zeneca is the world's number two cancer company in terms of drug sales behind Bristol Myers Squibb Co, with a declared aim of becoming number one.

The company has two prostate cancer drugs on the market, Zoladex and Casodex, and is to complete the acquistion of U.S. cancer care company Salick Health Care Inc later this month. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
